newsitem.title: USA: NIMO says no generator pact yet, but near.
newsitem.headline: NIMO says no generator pact yet, but near.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp said Thursday its proposal to buy out above-market cost power contracts is still in play despite its failure to reach an agreement by year-end as hoped.

"We've made a lot of progress and we're still hopeful that we'll have a negotiated settlement soon, but we don't have a deal yet," said Nicholas Ashooh, vice president of public affairs at Niagara Mohawk.

NIMO in August offered to terminate 44 independent power contracts in an effort to reverse the utility's weakening financial condition. The government-mandated contracts account for more than 90 percent of above-market cost to the utility.

The passing of the targeted date was no indication that negotiations had gone awry, Ashooh said. In October, chief executive officer William Davis said (he) remained hopeful an agreement would be reached by the end of 1996.
Ashooh on Thursday would only say NIMO is hopeful to "achieve something relatively soon."
The spokesman reiterated the proposal's importance to the implemention of its PowerChoice proposal which would introduce competitition and allow customers to choose their electricity supplier.

"We've got to solve (IPP contracts) before we can move on with PowerChoice," he said. "Otherwise feedback on PowerChoice has been very good and we believe when we get an agreement prospects for PowerChoice are really good."

The proposed buyout would not impair Niagara Mohawk's first mortgage bondholders, NIMO said. There were no specifics on how the buyout would be paid for except that it could be a combination of cash and securities, Ashooh said.
The offer would be made by a restructured Niagara Mohawk electric and natural gas transmission and distribution company.
